Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Reeza Hendricks and Temba Bavuma are the two openers for South Africa. Marcus Stoinis to start the proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

South Africa, on the other hand, will be very disappointed with their bowling effort. They took a pasting in the initial few overs but made a good comeback by picking up a few wickets to stop the momentum for a bit. However, Mitchell Marsh and Tim David made sure that they utilized the start they got and continued to find the boundaries. Lizaad Williams was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets while Marco Jansen, Tabraiz Shamsi, and Gerald Coetzee chipped in with one each. Their batters now have an uphill task to chase down this total and a few records need to be broken for them to get the win here. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

Australia got off to an absolute flier even though they lost Travis Head after he hit a six in the first over. Mitchell Marsh came in and started smashing it all around the park while Matthew Short also played a quick-fire 20 off just 11 balls. They ended the Powerplay on 70/3 but lost their way a bit by losing a couple of wickets in quick succession. Tim David joined in and then both he and Marsh attacked the Proteas bowlers left right and center. They added 97 runs together with David scoring a blistering 69 off just 28 balls. Aaron Hardie on debut also played a fine quick cameo of 23 off just 14 balls to take them over the 200-run mark while Marsh lost a bit of his timing towards the end but remained unbeaten on 92 off 49 balls to take them to a gigantic total here.

An absolutely breathtaking display of batting from the Aussies! This is the highest T20I total at Kingsmead, and Mitchell Marsh literally led them from the front with a brilliant unbeaten knock and they will surely be the happier side going into the break.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Another boundary! 20 runs off the over! Lungi Ngidi serves this a touch fuller and on middle, Mitchell Marsh goes for the lofted drive but his bat turns a bit when he connects. However, it still has enough power to go wide of mid on for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Goes short again and around off, Mitchell Marsh punches it through covers for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BOOM! 14 runs already in the over! Lungi Ngidi once again bangs this onto the pitch around middle and leg, Mitchell Marsh picks up the length early and pulls it over the deep mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Mitchell Marsh cuts hard but finds point this time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Two in two! Lungi Ngidi bowls this on a good length but on the pads, Mitchell Marsh heaves it towards the fine leg fence for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Mitchell Marsh greets Lungi Ngidi with a boundary! Ngidi begins with a short-of-a-length delivery, on middle, sits up nicely for the batter, Mitchell Marsh hoicks it towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Lungi Ngidi to Mitchell Marsh, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Lungi Ngidi will bowl from the other end.
Touch fuller and on middle, Matthew Short nudges it through backward square leg for a couple of runs. An eventful first over comes to an end!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Marco Jansen to Matthew Short, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and around off, Mitchell Marsh dabs it through point for a single and gets off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Marco Jansen to Mitchell Marsh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another length delivery down the leg side again, Mitchell Marsh looks to hook it away but misses again. It is called a wide. Jansen need to find the right line here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Marco Jansen to Mitchell Marsh, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: On a length but down the leg side, Mitchell Marsh misses his glance. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Marco Jansen to Mitchell Marsh, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length and on off, angling away, Mitchell Marsh withdraws is bat at the last moment as the ball goes past the outside edge to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Marco Jansen to Mitchell Marsh, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Skipper Mitchell Marsh comes in next.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Marco Jansen draws first blood! Six and out for Travis Head and very entertaining start to this game. This is on a hard length and on off, straightens a bit, Travis Head tries to poke at it with two minds and only manages to nick it behind towards first slip where Reeza Hendricks takes a fine low catch. Australia lose their first wicket!
Commentary.Howout: c Reeza Hendricks b Marco Jansen
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Marco Jansen to Travis Head, OUT! c Reeza Hendricks b Marco Jansen.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Travis Head and Australia are underway in some fashion! Marco Jansen lands this on a back of a length and outside off, Travis Head accepts the width on offer and slashes it over the deep backward point fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Marco Jansen to Travis Head, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Marco Jansen starts with a full delivery around off, shaping away, Travis Head goes for the big swing through the line but fails to connect.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Marco Jansen to Travis Head, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities and it is time for the all-important action in the middle. Matthew Short and Travis Head are the two openers for Australia. Marco Jansen will bowl the first over for South Africa.
It is time for the National Anthem of the respective sides with the Australian National Anthem up first.

PITCH REPORT-: Shaun Pollack is pitchside and says that the surface looks solid as the curator has put down new grass covering on this and will assist the pacers but the batters could trust the bounce on this surface. Adds that there will be a very good carry to the keeper and the surface is well-prepared for a T-20 game.

Mitchell Marsh, the captain of Australia says that they would have probably bowled first but don't mind batting either. Adds that they will look to set a good total on the board. Tells that this is the start of the T20I season before the World Cup next year. Mentions that there is a lot of cricket coming up and they are all excited about it. Says that they have players coming in from the Hundred and other competitions and have tried to keep a relaxed environment in the team. Hopes that they put on a good show here. Informs that Spencer Johnson, Aaron Hardie and Spencer Johnson are all making their debuts.

Aiden Markram, the skipper of South Africa says that they will bowl first. Adds that they are not sure how the wicket is going to play but they have a few players on their side who know the pitch and that is why they will look to chase here. Tells that the preparation has been good and the environment is nice as well. Mentions that they haven't done well as a team in recent times but they are ready for this series. Informs that two youngsters are making their debuts as Gerald Coetzee and Dewald Brevis are in the side.

Australia (Playing XI) - Matthew Short, Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh (C), Josh Inglis (WK), Marcus Stoinis, Tim David, Aaron Hardie (On Debut), Sean Abbott, Nathan Ellis, Tanveer Sangha (On Debut), Spencer Johnson (On Debut).

South Africa (Playing XI) - Temba Bavuma, Reeza Hendricks, Rassie van der Dussen, Aiden Markram (C), Dewald Brevis (On Debut), Tristan Stubbs (WK), Marco Jansen, Gerald Coetzee (On Debut), Lungi Ngidi, Lizaad Williams, Tabraiz Shamsi.
TOSS - South Africa have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

Australia, on the other hand, will be missing a lot of key players but this gives a chance to the others to make a mark. Mitchell Marsh is the skipper and the most in-form player for them and he also has a terrific record against South Africa. He will be key with both bat and ball. Matthew Short, Travis Head, and Marcus Stoinis make up a really strong batting order while Tim David has established himself as one of the best finishers in this format. Their bowling has been weakened with injuries but Spencer Johnson impressed with his pace and strength in the Men's Hundred 2023 and will be the one to watch out for while Sean Abbott, Jason Behrendorff, and Adam Zampa can use their experience to make a difference in this game. Let's see who comes out on top. Stay tuned for toss and team news.

South Africa hasn't been in great form in this format in recent times and will want to change that. Aiden Markram will lead the side and will be one of the key batters for them along with Rassie van der Dussen and Rassie van der Dussen. Dewald Brevis is an exciting addition to the squad and because of his ability to play shots all around the park, he is nicknamed 'Baby AB', and Tristan Stubbs will play the role of finisher for them. In the absence of regular starters, Lungi Ngidi and Tabraiz Shamsi will lead the bowling department with Marco Jansen. With the home crowd behind them, they will fancy their chances to get the win.

Hello and warm welcome folks! The stage is set for a three-match T20I series between two heavyweights South Africa and Australia and the first game will be played at Kingsmead in Durban. The Aussies have a superior record over the Proteas and will look to maintain that while the hosts hope to take an early lead in the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

With the ODI World Cup just a few weeks away, a T20I series would seem inconsequential, but not so when two powerhouses of the format, South Africa and Australia, meet. The men from Down Under have made the trip to the Rainbow Nation for what is going to be a highly competitive white-ball series. T20Is are not the only event on Australia's itinerary, as the three-match series will be followed by a five-match ODI series, which will serve as good preparation for both teams for the upcoming showpiece event in India. South African fans residing in Durban and fans of the sport in general are in for a treat as Kingsmead will host all three matches of the T20I series. The hosts, South Africa, led by Aiden Markram, have opted to rest some of the big names for this series in their quest to gauge the depth of talent in the T20I format. Their squad announcement was headlined by the maiden call-up of prodigy Dewald Brevis, who is touted as the next big thing in South African cricket. Temba Bavuma, on his return, will mark his presence at the top of the order along with Reeza Hendricks. Rassie van der Dussen, Aiden Markram, and Dewald Brevis will form the crux of the middle order. When it comes to wicket-keeping duties, it is a toss-up between Matthew Breetzke and Tristan Stubbs, but the latter is likely to get the nod. Their pace department is stacked with the likes of Marco Jansen, Sisanda Magala, Lungi Ngidi, Gerald Coetzee, and Lizaad Williams in the ranks. In what comes as a significant boost to their spin bowling stocks, left-arm spinner Keshav Maharaj will mark his comeback from injury through this series. Other than him, Bjorn Fortuin and Tabraiz Shamsi are the other spin options for the hosts. On the other hand, Australia will be seen in T20I action for the first time since they bowed out of the 2022 T20 World Cup in the group stage. In the absence of stalwarts like Pat Cummins, David Warner, and Steven Smith, Mitchell Marsh has been handed the reins for this series. Like South Africa, Australia have also given the opportunity to players who have impressed at the domestic level. The tourists were dealt a late blow in their preparations for this series as star all-rounder Glenn Maxwell incurred an ankle injury during the first training session in Durban. Matthew Wade has been named as his replacement but he will have to wait for his chance as Josh Inglis finds a spot in the playing XI announced a day before the game. Travis Head, Matthew Short and skipper Mitchell Marsh form the top three for the tourists, who will be expected to get off to a flying start. In the middle order, there will be no shortage of firepower with the presence of Marcus Stoinis, Tim David and Aaron Hardie. With Maxwell's exit from the squad, the spin bowling duties will pretty much rest on the shoulders of leggie Adam Zampa. The pace bowling unit has good depth, with uncapped Spencer Johnson providing the left-arm angle, while the right-arm duo of Sean Abbott and Nathan Ellis will keep the batters on their toes with their variations. Right then, the scene has been set for what promises to be an exciting series between two top sides. Who are you backing to draw the first blood at Kingsmead?
